title: Best AC Infinity Dehumidifier (2026): HYDRONE 3, 5 & 7
h1: The Best AC Infinity Dehumidifiers for Grow Tents
dek: AC Infinity’s HYDRONE line was built to live in a grow tent and talk to your controller. Here’s which size fits your setup — and when to look elsewhere.
description: The best AC Infinity dehumidifier for your grow tent: HYDRONE 3, HYDRONE 5 and HYDRONE 7 compared by tent size, draw rate, ducting and controller support.
intro: If your tent already runs on CLOUDLINE fans and a smart controller, an **AC Infinity dehumidifier** is the obvious next piece. The company’s HYDRONE plant dehumidifiers are designed specifically for grow tents: they have dual 6-inch duct ports, ten drying levels and a port that plugs into AC Infinity’s controllers, so humidity becomes one more line in the same app as your fans, lights and humidifier.

There are three sizes — HYDRONE 3, 5 and 7 — and AC Infinity rates them in a way that doesn’t line up neatly with the pint ratings on home dehumidifiers. Below we explain what those numbers mean, which HYDRONE suits which tent, how to set one up, and when a conventional compressor unit or a commercial machine is the better buy.
topPicksLead: The **AC Infinity HYDRONE 5** is the best fit for most growers: sized for typical 4×4 and 5×5 tents, ductable, and fully automated when paired with an AC Infinity controller.

products.name: AC Infinity HYDRONE 5 Plant Dehumidifier
pros: Sized for the most popular 4×4 and 5×5 tents
Dual 6-inch ports to duct dry air in or heat out
Ten drying levels for fine control
UIS port connects to AC Infinity smart controllers
cons: Small half-gallon tank without the drain hose
Rated differently from DOE pints, so comparisons are tricky
products.whyWeLoveIt: It’s the HYDRONE that fits the most tents. It’s small enough to sit inside or beside a 4×4, strong enough to hold a flowering canopy in range, and when you plug it into an AC Infinity controller it can follow your humidity or VPD targets automatically instead of running at a fixed speed.
products.performance: AC Infinity lists a real-world draw rate of about 4 liters a day — roughly 8.5 pints — and notes that it isn’t directly comparable to compressor ratings. It runs on 120 volts, draws between about 209 and 350 watts depending on its level, and is listed for 45°F to 95°F. The internal tank holds about half a gallon, so most growers attach the drain hose and forget about emptying it.
products.notes: AC Infinity has marketed it for 2–3 plants, 4×4 and up to 5×5 tents at different times; treat 5×5 as the upper limit for a dense, heavily watered canopy.

products.name: AC Infinity HYDRONE 7 Plant Dehumidifier
pros: About double the HYDRONE 5’s draw rate
cons: Taller cabinet takes floor space inside a tent
Draws about 610 watts — plan your circuit
products.whyWeLoveIt: Big tents full of flowering plants push out a lot of water, especially right after lights-off. The HYDRONE 7 is AC Infinity’s answer, with roughly twice the drying power of the 5 and its own onboard controller for humidity and VPD targets.
products.performance: AC Infinity lists a real-world draw rate of about 8 liters a day, or roughly 17 pints, and a power draw of about 610 watts on 120 volts. Its listings put coverage at up to 8×8 or 10×10 tents. That’s a lot of heat in an enclosed space, so most growers duct its exhaust out of the tent or run it outside and duct dry air in.

products.name: AC Infinity HYDRONE 3 Plant Dehumidifier
pros: Sized for 2×2 tents and small cabinets
Intake fan mode and dual ducting
cons: Not enough for a full 4×4 in flower
Fewer published specs than its bigger siblings
products.whyWeLoveIt: A 2×2 or small grow cabinet needs fine humidity control more than raw capacity. The HYDRONE 3 gives you the same ten-level, VPD-aware approach as the bigger models in a size that won’t crowd a small tent.
products.performance: AC Infinity positions it for tents up to about 2×2, which suits one or two plants or a seedling and clone setup. It shares the line’s dual-duct design and intake fan mode. If you’re planning to move up to a 3×3 or 4×4, buy the HYDRONE 5 now rather than outgrowing this one in a season.

products.name: Quest Dual 155 Overhead Dehumidifier
products.award: Best for grow rooms beyond a tent

Hangs overhead to save floor space

products.whyWeLoveIt: Once you’re running several tents in one room or converting a spare room into a grow, a single commercial unit outperforms a row of tent dehumidifiers. The Dual 155 is the usual first step up.
products.performance: Quest rates it at 155 pints a day at 80°F and 60% humidity on about 8 amps at 115 volts. It drains continuously and can hang from the ceiling. See the full lineup in our [Quest dehumidifier](/best/best-quest-dehumidifier/) guide.

sections.heading: The HYDRONE line, by the numbers

blocks.text: Those draw rates look small next to a “50-pint” basement dehumidifier, but the numbers aren’t measured the same way. Home units are rated under a standardized DOE test at 65°F; AC Infinity quotes what it says the HYDRONE pulls in typical tent conditions. The practical takeaway: pick a HYDRONE by tent size and plant count rather than by comparing pints, and use our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) if you’re weighing a conventional unit instead.

sections.heading: How we pick AC Infinity dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don’t run a grow lab. We compared AC Infinity’s published specs and product listings — draw rate, power, operating range, ducting and controller support — and noted where the company’s own coverage claims have shifted. We then read grower feedback for recurring themes: how well each size holds humidity after lights-off, heat added to the tent, drain-hose reliability and how smoothly the units integrate with AC Infinity controllers.
We ranked the HYDRONE 5 first because it fits the most common tent sizes. We also included one commercial unit, because past a certain size, no tent dehumidifier is the right tool.

sections.heading: What to look for in an AC Infinity dehumidifier

items.label: Tent size and plant count
items.text: A 2×2 suits the HYDRONE 3, 3×3 to 5×5 the HYDRONE 5, and larger tents the HYDRONE 7. Dense canopies and heavy watering push you up a size.

items.label: Your controller
items.text: If you already use an AC Infinity smart controller, the HYDRONE’s UIS port lets it follow humidity or VPD targets and log data in the app.

items.label: Heat management
items.text: Every dehumidifier releases heat. Use the 6-inch ports to vent warm exhaust out of the tent, especially in summer.

items.label: Drainage
items.text: The tanks are small, so plan a gravity drain to a bucket or reservoir set lower than the unit.

items.label: A second hygrometer
items.text: Place an independent sensor at canopy height to confirm what the controller reports. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) explains why built-in sensors drift.

sections.heading: How to set up a HYDRONE in your tent

items: **Decide inside or outside.** Inside is simplest. Outside keeps heat and floor space out of the tent; duct dry air in through one 6-inch port and vent exhaust away from the intake.
**Raise it and run the drain.** Set the unit on a stand so the hose runs downhill to a bucket or drain, and check the hose isn’t kinked.
**Connect the controller.** Plug the UIS cable into your AC Infinity controller and choose humidity or VPD mode.
**Set targets by stage.** Common starting points are about 65–70% for seedlings and clones, 50–60% in veg and 40–50% in flower, dropping a little in the final weeks.
**Watch the lights-off spike.** Humidity jumps when lights go off and temperatures fall. If the unit can’t catch up within an hour or so, add capacity or ventilation.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.text: Prolonged high humidity in a dense flowering canopy is the classic setup for bud rot and powdery mildew. Our [dehumidifiers and mold](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-help-with-mold/) guide explains how humidity control fits into prevention.

sections.heading: When to choose something other than a HYDRONE

items: **You want the most pints for the money.** A conventional compressor dehumidifier placed outside the tent and ducted in can remove more water per dollar; our [grow tent dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-grow-tent/) guide covers those options.
**You’re drying a whole room or several tents.** Step up to a commercial unit like the Quest Dual 155.
**You’re growing houseplants, not a tent.** A small home unit is simpler; see our [dehumidifier for plants](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-plants/) picks.
**Your tent is too dry, not too wet.** That’s a humidifier job — AC Infinity makes those too, and our [dehumidifier vs. humidifier](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-humidifier/) guide explains the difference.

blocks.text: For most growers, the **AC Infinity HYDRONE 5** is the one to buy: it suits 4×4 and 5×5 tents, ducts cleanly and automates beautifully with an AC Infinity controller. Choose the **AC Infinity HYDRONE 7** for 8×8 and 10×10 tents, the **AC Infinity HYDRONE 3** for a 2×2 or cabinet, and a **Quest Dual 155** once your grow outgrows tents altogether.

faqs.q: Is the AC Infinity dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: If you already use AC Infinity fans and a smart controller, yes. The HYDRONE line is built for tents, with ducting ports and controller integration that let humidity run on autopilot. If you only want maximum water removal per dollar, a conventional compressor unit can be cheaper.

faqs.q: How many pints does the AC Infinity HYDRONE 5 remove?
faqs.a: AC Infinity lists a real-world draw rate of about 4 liters a day, roughly 8.5 pints, and says it isn’t directly comparable to standard compressor ratings.

faqs.q: HYDRONE 5 or HYDRONE 7: which should I buy?
faqs.a: The HYDRONE 5 fits most 4×4 and 5×5 tents. The HYDRONE 7 has about twice the draw rate and a built-in VPD controller, and suits 8×8 to 10×10 tents or very heavy flowering loads.

faqs.q: Is the HYDRONE 3 enough for a 4×4 tent?
faqs.a: Generally no. AC Infinity sizes the HYDRONE 3 for tents up to about 2×2. For a 4×4, choose the HYDRONE 5.

faqs.q: Does the HYDRONE work with AC Infinity controllers?
faqs.a: Yes. The HYDRONE 5 has a UIS port for AC Infinity smart controllers, which enables app control, humidity and VPD automations and data logging. The HYDRONE 7 also has its own built-in humidity and VPD controller.

faqs.q: Does an AC Infinity dehumidifier need a drain?
faqs.a: Not strictly, but the tank holds only about half a gallon, so most growers connect the gravity drain hose to a lower bucket or drain to avoid frequent emptying.
